Specify the problem to find your solution. {I assume the problem in question is censorship.} Older sites suffered because the product got popular and the owner was tempted with monetary incentives. {Bills must be paid and there's room to put a little cash in yo pockets, when advertisers/celebrities/people with money and agendas want to be featured.} Taking outside money gives them influence. {If you want to pay this month's server bill or get a bonus for your wallet, quiet down those FPH} Therefore, private ownership -> outside money -> outside influence -> censorship. You can cut this short at any of the first 3 steps in order to prevent the outcome.

Although, censorship can also come because owners get ideologically persuaded to defect. {Moot} Therefore private ownership is only as secure as the owner is.

A) Change ownership into a form that isn't easy to be corrupted. Few individuals are incorruptable, groups of people are messy, and I assume Atko trusts himself more than he trusts outsiders, so this is a difficult step to intervene. B) Outside money can be circumvented by distributing where the money originates- if bitcoin donations are sufficient, problem solved. If we can spread out patronship so that no one has large influence, that'd be good too. C) Outside influence is derived from money, so if we can find "benevolent patrons" who float voat but don't intervene, that'd be awesome. But not very feasible.

Now, there's a bunch of things that older sites got wrong: moderator management, admin-mod relations, community atmosphere, etc. Some of those get affected by my breakdown, some don't. But when it comes down to it, if we allow untrustworthy people to influence voat, we'll find censorship like any other site. A more broad system of ownership sounds great in my head, but on paper, it doesn't play out. The financial aspect of voat, though, is something we can collectively manage. That's how we can keep our site clean.

TL;DR - whoever pays for voat controls voat. Let's keep control of our site.

"Concerning the contrivance and mode of his death, the common account is this. The conspirators being in some doubt when and where they should attack him, whether while he was in the bath, or at supper, Stephanus, a steward of Domitilla's, then under prosecution for defrauding his mistress, offered them his advice and assistance; and wrapping up his left arm, as if it was hurt, in wool and bandages for some days, to prevent suspicion, at the hour appointed, he secreted a dagger in them. Pretending then to make a discovery of a conspiracy, and being for that reason admitted, he presented to the emperor a memorial, and while he was reading it in great astonishment, stabbed him in the groin. But Domitian, though wounded, making resistance, Clodianus, one of his guards, Maximus, a freedman of Parthenius's, Saturius, his principal chamberlain, with some gladiators, fell upon him, and stabbed him in seven places. A boy who had the charge of the Lares in his bed-chamber, and was then in attendance as usual, gave these further particulars: that he was ordered by Domitian, upon receiving his first wound, to reach him a dagger which lay under his pillow, and call in his domestics; but that he found nothing at the head of the bed, excepting the hilt of a poniard, and that all the doors were fastened: that the emperor in the mean time got hold of Stephanus, and throwing him upon the ground, struggled a long time with him; one while endeavouring to wrench the dagger from him, another while, though his fingers were miserably mangled, to tear out his eyes. He was slain upon the fourteenth of the calends of October [18th Sept.], in the forty-fifth year of his age, and the fifteenth of his reign."
